decisions.title: Canonical locale identity
decisions.issue: Valid language tags can preserve caller spelling or use one registry-aware identity, and aliases can otherwise become distinct map keys.
interpretations: canonicalize every stored key through the pinned locale dependency.
decisions.peer_behavior: no independent local differential harness is claimed.
decisions.selected_behavior: Every stored and queried locale is canonicalized before identity comparison, ordering, hashing, persistence, or encoding.
decisions.rationale: One canonical identity prevents aliases and casing variants from representing different translations.
decisions.security_consequences: Malformed, invalid UTF-8, and overlong locale text fails before retention.
decisions.resource_consequences: Canonicalization is bounded by the locale dependency and performs no network access.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Preferred-value or registry-table changes require dependency, persistence, and release review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Encoders emit canonical locale keys rather than accepted aliases or caller casing.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 5646 errata and the current IANA registry are monitored separately from the pinned locale dependency snapshot.
decisions.reconsider_when: BCP 47, its errata, the IANA registry, or the locale dependency changes canonical identity semantics.

decisions.title: Special and private-use locale acceptance
interpretations: accept valid tags by default and expose explicit construction policy.
decisions.peer_behavior: Locale libraries generally parse these valid classes but do not define application acceptance policy.
decisions.rationale: Syntax validity and application acceptance are separate decisions.
decisions.security_consequences: Applications can fail closed for classes their authorization or persistence model does not recognize.
decisions.resource_consequences: Policy evaluation is bounded and performs no registry lookup or I/O.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Default acceptance remains stable; tightening requires an explicit caller policy or compatibility review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Accepted classes serialize as their canonical BCP 47 identity.
decisions.upstream_status: No BCP 47 rule selects one application acceptance policy for valid special classes.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported application profile makes one class mandatory or forbidden.

decisions.title: Duplicate identity after canonicalization
decisions.issue: Distinct input spellings can canonicalize to the same locale and silently overwrite a translation.
interpretations: reject unless an explicit duplicate policy selects a winner.
decisions.peer_behavior: Generic maps commonly overwrite duplicates, but that behavior does not expose canonical identity collisions.
decisions.selected_behavior: Strict construction rejects canonical duplicate locales; explicit construction options may select left-wins or right-wins behavior.
decisions.rationale: Silent overwrite can hide conflicting localized content or parser differentials.
decisions.security_consequences: Canonical duplicate smuggling fails closed by default.
decisions.resource_consequences: Duplicate detection is bounded by the locale-count limit.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Existing strict callers retain rejection; permissive resolution requires an explicit policy.
decisions.wire_consequences: Strict JSON rejects duplicate raw members and distinct members that canonicalize to one locale.
decisions.upstream_status: BCP 47 defines tag identity but not an application map's collision policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported wire profile defines deterministic duplicate handling that must be preserved.

decisions.title: Exact lookup and language matching separation
decisions.issue: Exact locale identity, RFC lookup, and implementation-defined best-fit matching produce observably different results.
interpretations: keep exact lookup separate and expose matching as an explicit operation.
decisions.peer_behavior: pinned implementation dependency rather than independent peer evidence.
decisions.selected_behavior: performs explicit weighted matching against the current supported locale set.
decisions.rationale: Callers can distinguish stored identity from a selected alternative and cannot receive an invented translation implicitly.
decisions.security_consequences: Exact authorization or persistence lookups cannot be widened by matching.
decisions.resource_consequences: Candidate count is bounded and matching performs no network access.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Matcher-data updates require governed vectors and compatibility review even when APIs compile unchanged.
decisions.wire_consequences: Matching returns the actual stored locale and text; it does not rewrite the stored map.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 4647 errata and pinned matcher behavior are reviewed separately; no full RFC conformance claim is made for best-fit results.
decisions.reconsider_when: The package adopts a versioned RFC 4647 lookup profile or replaces its matcher.

decisions.title: Explicit fallback ownership
decisions.issue: Parent traversal, application fallback chains, and a final default locale are not one universal standards-defined policy.
interpretations: Infer parents and a global default automatically.
require callers to construct a bounded immutable plan.
decisions.peer_behavior: Locale libraries expose parent relationships but cannot select an application's fallback graph or default.
decisions.selected_behavior: Fallback occurs only through an explicit bounded plan whose candidate kinds, chains, and optional default are caller-owned.
decisions.rationale: Explicit plans prevent ambient global locale policy and invented translations.
decisions.security_consequences: Cycles, duplicates, invalid candidates, and oversized plans fail before resolution.
decisions.resource_consequences: Plan size and traversal are bounded and immutable.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Application fallback order remains explicit and independent of exact lookup and best-fit matching.
decisions.wire_consequences: Resolution returns an existing stored entry and never serializes an inferred translation.
decisions.upstream_status: No upstream standard defines this package's application fallback graph.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported application profile supplies a normative fallback chain.

decisions.title: Accept-Language quality and wildcard policy
decisions.issue: Equal quality values, zero quality, wildcard selection, duplicate canonical ranges, and unsupported ranges require deterministic local policy.
interpretations: Reorder equal weights, treat zero as acceptable, or let wildcard select any map iteration result.
preserve input order, exclude zero, and select wildcard deterministically.
decisions.peer_behavior: HTTP frameworks differ in normalization and wildcard policy; no maintained peer is asserted as normative.
decisions.selected_behavior: Parsing preserves stable order within equal weights, excludes zero-weight preferences from selection, rejects canonical duplicates, and lets wildcard choose the first canonical lexical stored locale.
decisions.rationale: Stable ordering and lexical wildcard selection prevent runtime map order from affecting responses.
decisions.security_consequences: Header bytes, candidate count, grammar, parameters, and quality precision are bounded and validated.
decisions.resource_consequences: Parsing and selection are bounded and perform no I/O.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Tie and wildcard results are documented behavior and require compatibility review if changed.
decisions.wire_consequences: No default locale is added; an empty or wholly unacceptable header yields a missing result.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9110 and RFC 4647 errata are monitored; wildcard tie-breaking remains package policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported HTTP profile mandates different quality, duplicate, or wildcard behavior.

decisions.title: Canonical JSON object mapping
decisions.issue: JSON objects are unordered and duplicate member behavior is unpredictable, while localized values need deterministic bytes and collision-safe keys.
interpretations: Use generic map encoding and last-wins decoding.
sort canonical keys and reject every raw or canonical duplicate.
decisions.peer_behavior: Generic JSON decoders vary in duplicate handling and do not enforce BCP 47 canonical-key collisions.
decisions.selected_behavior: Encoding emits one compact object with canonical locale keys in lexical order; strict decoding rejects duplicates, invalid UTF-8, invalid locales, trailing values, and limit violations.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic bytes support stable hashes and fixtures while fail-closed decoding prevents member shadowing.
decisions.security_consequences: Duplicate, invalid, oversized, and ambiguous input fails without disclosing localized content.
decisions.resource_consequences: Input, locale count, locale bytes, text bytes, and total retained bytes are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Canonical byte order and strict rejection are public compatibility commitments.
decisions.wire_consequences: Missing text is an absent member and present-empty text is an empty JSON string.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 8259 errata are monitored; the canonical ordering profile is package-owned.
decisions.reconsider_when: A versioned canonical JSON profile replaces this package-specific byte contract.

decisions.title: Legacy JSON compatibility boundary
decisions.issue: Existing payloads may use JSON null or underscore locale separators even though neither is the canonical localized representation.
interpretations: isolate them behind an explicit decode mode.
decisions.peer_behavior: Legacy application serializers commonly emit these forms, but no maintained-peer conformance claim is made.
decisions.rationale: Compatibility input does not silently weaken the default parser or persist a second wire identity.
decisions.security_consequences: Permissive mode retains all ordinary duplicate, UTF-8, locale, and resource checks.
decisions.resource_consequences: Legacy normalization is bounded and performs no I/O.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers must opt into legacy acceptance and can migrate stored data by canonical re-encoding.
decisions.wire_consequences: Output never emits null or underscore locale separators.
decisions.upstream_status: This is a package migration policy, not an RFC 8259 or BCP 47 requirement.
decisions.reconsider_when: Legacy payloads are retired or a versioned wire format requires continued acceptance.
